items.subject: Researchers trick Fortune-500 AI agents into running arbitrary code via llms.txt
items.what_happened: Researchers demonstrated indirect prompt-injection supply-chain attacks in which malicious instructions embedded in llms.txt guidance files caused AI agents at Fortune-500 companies to execute arbitrary code. Operators running self-hosted agent stacks should treat llms.txt and other fetched documentation as untrusted data, not instructions, and sandbox or gate any tool/code-execution path driven by retrieved content.
items.why_it_matters: Classified as breaking for on-prem operators: action may be required on llms.txt, mcp, agent-frameworks
items.rationale: Assess exposure before the next upgrade window
